subtitle: A creation episode in Spence's Mexican synthesis

sun.excerpt: The myth of Nanahuatl tells how before the sun was created humanity dwelt in sable and horrid gloom. Only a human sacrifice could hasten the appearance of the luminary. Metztli (The Moon) led forth Nanahuatl as a sacrifice, and he was cast upon a funeral pyre, in the flames of which he was consumed. Metztli also cast herself upon the mass of flame, and with her death the sun rose above the horizon.
sun.note: Verbatim prose from Lewis Spence's early twentieth-century synthesis, not a direct translation of the Indigenous source material he discusses. Preserve its dated, colonial framing.

narrativeBlocks.title: A world in darkness
narrativeBlocks.body: Spence's account says humanity lived in darkness before the sun appeared. Nanahuatl is led as a sacrifice and cast onto a funeral pyre.

narrativeBlocks.title: The sun rises
narrativeBlocks.body: Quotation from Spence's English prose synthesis (whitespace normalized): “The myth of Nanahuatl tells how before the sun was created humanity dwelt in sable and horrid gloom. Only a human sacrifice could hasten the appearance of the luminary. Metztli (The Moon) led forth Nanahuatl as a sacrifice, and he was cast upon a funeral pyre, in the flames of which he was consumed. Metztli also cast herself upon the mass of flame, and with her death the sun rose above the horizon.”

narrativeBlocks.title: The moon also enters the story
narrativeBlocks.body: In this version, Metztli also casts herself onto the flames, after which the sun rises. The lesson follows Spence's account rather than merging it with other creation narratives.

narrativeBlocks.title: A twentieth-century synthesis
narrativeBlocks.body: Lewis Spence's early twentieth-century book summarizes Mexican, Maya, and Peruvian material. This passage is Spence's English account, not a direct translation from a named Nahuatl manuscript.

narrativeBlocks.title: Name the tradition in view
narrativeBlocks.body: This episode is presented in Spence's Mexican mythology chapter; it is not evidence for every Mesoamerican people or every account of the sun's origin.
